Vandiyathevan.description: A young warrior of the Vaanar clan, Vandiyathevan is the protagonist of the story, entrusted with a secret mission by Prince Aditya Karikalan and known for his wit and bravery.

Pazhuvettaraiyar.description: The elder Pazhuvettaraiyar is a powerful noble and military leader in the Chola Empire, serving as Treasurer and Keeper of the Granaries, and is second in authority only to the emperor.

Aditya Karikalan.description: The crown prince of the Chola Empire and Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Armies, Aditya Karikalan is Vandiyathevan's friend and the one who entrusts him with a secret mission.

Thirumunaippadi.description: A region in southern India, located between Thondai Nadu and Chola Nadu, significant in the Chola period.

Thondai Nadu.description: A historical region in Tamilakam, north of Chola Nadu, once ruled by the Pallavas.

Chola Nadu.description: The heartland of the Chola dynasty, a powerful South Indian kingdom.

Chidambaram.description: A sacred temple town in Tamil Nadu, famous for its Nataraja temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Veeranarayana Lake.description: A vast man-made lake near Chidambaram, constructed by the Cholas for irrigation and prosperity.

Veeranarayanam Lake.description: An alternate, shortened name for Veeranarayana Lake.

Aadi.description: A Tamil month (mid-July to mid-August) associated with monsoon and agricultural festivals.

Avani.description: A Tamil month (mid-August to mid-September), following Aadi.

Vaanar clan.description: A noble warrior clan in Tamilakam, to which Vandiyathevan belongs.

Tamilakam.description: The ancient geographical region of the Tamil people, encompassing present-day Tamil Nadu and surrounding areas.

Aadi Perukku.description: A Tamil festival celebrated on the 18th day of Aadi, marking the rising of rivers and prosperity.

Vadakaveri.description: A name for the northern branch of the Kaveri River, considered sacred by devotees.

Kollidam.description: The common name for the northern branch of the Kaveri River.

Vadavaru.description: A river or canal that branches from the Kaveri and feeds into the Veeranarayana Lake.

Pallava.description: A South Indian dynasty that ruled parts of Tamilakam before the Cholas.

Madurai.description: A major city in southern Tamil Nadu, historically significant and often contested by dynasties.

Rajaditya.description: A Chola prince, son of Parantaka, known for his valor and for building the Veeranarayana Lake.

Takkolam.description: A historic battlefield where Prince Rajaditya fought and died heroically.

Chola dynasty.description: A powerful and influential South Indian royal family that ruled Tamilakam for centuries.

Pazhuvettaraiyars.description: A noble clan allied with the Cholas, known for their martial prowess and right to bear the palmyra flag.

Pazhuvur.description: The city associated with the Pazhuvettaraiyar clan, near Uraiyur.

Uraiyur.description: An ancient city and former capital of the early Cholas, located on the banks of the Kaveri.

Vijayalaya Cholan.description: The founder of the imperial Chola dynasty, renowned for his military achievements.

Aditya Cholan.description: Son of Vijayalaya Cholan, known for building Shiva temples and expanding the Chola kingdom.

Parantaka Chola Maharaja.description: A celebrated Chola king, son of Aditya Cholan, famous for his military conquests.

Pandyas.description: A rival South Indian dynasty, often in conflict with the Cholas.

Cheras.description: Another major South Indian dynasty, contemporaneous with the Cholas and Pandyas.

Lanka.description: The island kingdom south of India, present-day Sri Lanka, invaded by the Cholas.

Tanjore.description: The capital city of the Chola Empire, also known as Thanjavur.

Kadambur Samburayar.description: A local chieftain or noble whose palace Vandiyathevan plans to visit.

Kanchi.description: A historic city (Kanchipuram) in Tamil Nadu, once a major center of learning and capital of the Pallavas.

Sundara Chola.description: The reigning emperor of the Chola dynasty during the events of the novel.

Kalinga.description: A historical region in eastern India, referenced as the northern extent of the Pazhuvettaraiyars' fame.

Eelam.description: The Tamil name for the island of Sri Lanka, referenced as the southern extent of the Pazhuvettaraiyars' fame.

league.description: An old unit of distance, roughly equivalent to 3 miles or 4.8 kilometers.

bund.description: An embankment or levee built to contain or control water in a lake or river.

sluices.description: Channels or gates for controlling the flow of water from a reservoir or lake.

karuvelam.description: A type of hardy tree (Prosopis juliflora) commonly planted for erosion control.

vilva.description: A sacred tree (Aegle marmelos) in Hindu tradition, often planted near temples and water bodies.

palanquins.description: Covered litters or carriages, usually carried by bearers, used for transporting people.

areca palm leaves.description: Leaves from the areca palm tree, traditionally used as plates for serving food.

thazhamboo.description: A fragrant flower (screw pine or pandanus) used for hair decoration in South India.

sevandhi.description: Chrysanthemum flowers, commonly used for garlands and hair adornment.

mullai.description: Jasmine flowers, highly valued for their fragrance and used in garlands.

iruvatchi.description: A type of flower used for decoration, specific to Tamil culture.

champakam.description: A fragrant yellow flower (Michelia champaca), often used in South Indian rituals and adornment.

kummi.description: A traditional Tamil folk dance performed by women, involving rhythmic clapping and singing.

sindhu.description: A genre of Tamil folk song, often performed during festivals and celebrations.

Azhwarkkadiyan Nambi.description: A devout Vaishnavite spy and philosopher, known for his sharp wit and debating skills; he plays a recurring role in the story as both comic relief and a key informant.

Parantaka Sundara Chola Maharaja.description: The reigning Chola emperor, renowned for his valor and beauty; father of Princess Kundavai.

Kundavai.description: The intelligent and influential princess of the Chola dynasty, daughter of Sundara Chola.

Aditya.description: Prince Aditya Karikalan, the Chola crown prince and commander who entrusts Vandiyathevan with a secret mission.

Azhwarkkadiyan.description: Another reference to Azhwarkkadiyan Nambi, the Vaishnavite debater.

Patha Thooli Pattar.description: A Shaivite priest and one of the disputants in the religious debate with Azhwarkkadiyan.

Vallavaraiyan.description: Another name for Vandiyathevan, used interchangeably in the text.

Periya Pazhuvettaraiyar.description: A powerful and senior nobleman, the Lord of the Granary, renowned for his military prowess and high status in the Chola court.

Chola.description: A powerful South Indian dynasty that ruled over much of southern India during the 10th century.

Ponni.description: Another name for the Kaveri river, revered in Tamil literature and central to the Chola kingdom.

Kaveri.description: The sacred river flowing through the Chola country, vital for agriculture and culture.

Pazhaiyarai.description: The capital city of the Chola kings during this period, known for its grandeur and temples.

Poompuhar.description: An ancient port city of the Cholas, now reduced to a village in the story's timeline.

gopurams.description: Towering gateways of South Indian temples, often elaborately decorated.

Thevaram.description: A collection of devotional hymns dedicated to Lord Shiva, sung in Tamil temples.

Thiruvaimozhi.description: A revered collection of Tamil hymns composed by the Vaishnavite saint Nammalvar, sung in Vishnu temples.

Kadambur.description: A town or village that Vandiyathevan aims to reach before sunset.

Veera Narayanapuram Vinnagara.description: A Vishnu temple near Kadambur, site of the festival and religious debate.

Aadi Thirumanjanam.description: A special festival celebrated in the Tamil month of Aadi, involving ritual bathing of deities.

Vaishnavite.description: A devotee of Lord Vishnu, following the Vaishnava tradition.

Shaivite.description: A devotee of Lord Shiva, following the Shaiva tradition.

Advaita Vedantin.description: A follower of the Advaita Vedanta philosophy, which teaches non-dualism and the unity of the soul with Brahman.

Sannyasi.description: A Hindu ascetic who has renounced worldly life, often wearing ochre robes.

Thirumal.description: A Tamil name for Lord Vishnu.

Ravana.description: The ten-headed king of Lanka and antagonist in the Ramayana, who received boons from Shiva.

Lord Rama.description: An avatar of Vishnu and hero of the Ramayana, who defeated Ravana.

Brahma.description: The Hindu god of creation, part of the Trimurti along with Vishnu and Shiva.

Shiva.description: One of the principal Hindu deities, worshipped as the supreme god by Shaivites.

Vishnu.description: One of the principal Hindu deities, worshipped as the supreme god by Vaishnavites.

Vedanta.description: A school of Hindu philosophy based on the teachings of the Upanishads.

Brahman.description: The ultimate, formless reality in Hindu philosophy, especially in Advaita Vedanta.

Sri Shankara Bhagavatpada.description: Also known as Adi Shankaracharya, a philosopher and theologian who consolidated the doctrine of Advaita Vedanta.

Brahmasutra Bhashya.description: A commentary on the Brahmasutras, written by Adi Shankaracharya.

Shankaracharya.description: A title for Adi Shankara, the great Advaita philosopher.

Upanishads.description: Ancient Hindu scriptures that form the philosophical basis of Vedanta.

Bhagavad Gita.description: A sacred Hindu scripture, part of the Mahabharata, teaching spiritual wisdom.

Brahmasutras.description: A foundational text of Vedanta philosophy.

Bhaja Govindam.description: A famous devotional hymn composed by Adi Shankaracharya, urging devotion to Lord Krishna.

Munkudumi Nambi.description: A nickname for Azhwarkkadiyan Nambi, possibly referring to his distinctive hair tuft.

Swamigal.description: A respectful term for a holy man or ascetic.

Veerasaiva.description: A follower of the Veerashaiva tradition, a sect within Shaivism.

Kannan.description: A Tamil name for Lord Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu.

Krishna.description: An avatar of Vishnu, central figure in Hindu mythology.

Gopis.description: The cowherd maidens of Vrindavan, devotees of Krishna.

Paramasivan.description: A reverential name for Lord Shiva.

Lord of the Granary.description: A title for Periya Pazhuvettaraiyar, indicating his responsibility over the royal granaries.

palanquin.description: A covered litter for one passenger, carried on poles by bearers.

kumudams.description: A type of aquatic plant, often referring to white water lilies found in South Indian rivers and ponds.

ochre robes.description: Saffron-colored garments traditionally worn by Hindu ascetics and monks.

mantras.description: Sacred chants or incantations believed to have spiritual power.

Swami.description: A term of respect for a Hindu ascetic or spiritual teacher.

avatar.description: A divine incarnation or descent of a deity, especially Vishnu, into earthly form.

punnai.description: A type of flowering tree (Calophyllum inophyllum) common in South India.

konnai.description: The golden shower tree (Cassia fistula), known for its yellow blossoms.

kadamba.description: A flowering tree (Neolamarckia cadamba) with fragrant round blossoms, sacred in Indian tradition.

jaggery.description: Unrefined cane sugar, commonly used in South Indian cuisine and rituals.

flattened rice.description: Rice that has been parboiled, flattened, and dried, used as a snack or offering.

puffed rice.description: Rice grains that have been expanded by roasting, often eaten as a snack or used in offerings.

betel leaves.description: Leaves of the betel plant, commonly chewed with areca nut in South Asia.

eaglewood.description: A fragrant wood used in incense and perfumes, also known as agarwood.

sandalwood.description: A fragrant wood used for carvings, incense, and religious rituals in India.

throng.description: A large, densely packed crowd of people.

barracks.description: Buildings used to house soldiers, especially in a royal or military context.

Periya Pazhuvettarayar.description: A powerful and senior commander in the Chola Empire, head of the Pazhuvettaraiyar clan, and a key figure in the royal court's politics.

Tandavarayan.description: A member of Pazhuvettarayar’s retinue, mentioned here as a soldier who tries to mount Vandiyathevan’s horse.

Sambuvarayar.description: The lord of Kadambur, a local chieftain and ally of the Cholas, whose palace is a center for political gatherings.

Kandhamaaran.description: Son of Sambuvarayar and a close friend of Vandiyathevan.

Iswara Munigal.description: The chief priest of the Veeranarayana Perumal temple, depicted as a saintly and devoted figure.

Iswarapattar.description: Another name for the chief priest of the Veeranarayana Perumal temple, possibly the same as Iswara Munigal.

Nathamunigal.description: A young boy in this chapter, destined to become the first in the line of Vaishnava acharyas, later famed for collecting the hymns of Nammazhwar.

Parantaka Chola.description: Grandson of Vijayalaya Chola, a celebrated Chola king known for expanding the empire and roofing the Chidambaram temple with gold.

Pazhuvettarayar.description: A powerful noble clan in the Chola Empire, with Periya Pazhuvettarayar as its head.

Mutharaiyar of Thanjavur.description: Refers to the former ruling clan of Thanjavur, defeated by the Cholas about a century earlier.

Cholas.description: The ruling dynasty of southern India during the novel, known for their military prowess and cultural achievements.

Thanjavur.description: A major city and capital of the Chola Empire.

Paluvur.description: A region or locality associated with the Pazhuvettarayar clan.

Kadambur palace.description: The residence of Sambuvarayar, where significant political gatherings take place.

Saivite.description: A devotee of Shiva, one of the two main sects in Tamil religious life, often contrasted with Vaishnavites.

Kuravai dance.description: A traditional Tamil folk dance, often performed during temple festivals and celebrations.

Vinnagara temple.description: A temple dedicated to Vishnu, also referred to as Veeranarayana Perumal temple in this chapter.

Veeranarayana Perumal.description: A form of the god Vishnu, the presiding deity of the temple at Veeranarayanapuram.

Andal.description: A revered female saint and poet of the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition, whose hymns are sung during festivals.

Nammazhwar.description: One of the twelve Alwars, saint-poets of the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition, credited with composing the Tamil Veda.

Vijayalaya Chola.description: Founder of the Chola dynasty’s imperial line, grandfather of Parantaka Chola.

Kopperakesari.description: An honorific title of Parantaka Chola, meaning 'Lion among Kings.'

Chola Chikamani.description: An honorific title meaning 'Jewel among the Cholas.'

Sura Chikamani.description: An honorific title meaning 'Jewel among the brave.'

Rashtrakuta.description: A powerful dynasty from the Deccan region, rivals of the Cholas.

Manyakheta.description: The capital city of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.

Veeranarayanapuram.description: A town established on the banks of Veeranarayana Lake, site of the Vishnu temple.

Vinnagaram.description: A Tamil term for Vishnugriham, meaning 'celestial abode of Vishnu.'

Sri Narayana Murthi.description: A title for Vishnu, the presiding deity of the temple.

Kurugur.description: The birthplace of Nammazhwar, also known as Alwarthirunagari.

Sadagopan.description: Another name for Nammazhwar, the saint-poet.

Azhwar.description: A title for the twelve saint-poets of the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition.

Vaishnava.description: A follower of Vishnu, one of the two main sects in Tamil religious life.

Aalavandhaar.description: A famous Vaishnava acharya, descendant of Nathamunigal.

Sri Ramanuja.description: A preeminent Vaishnava philosopher and acharya, known for organizing the Sri Vaishnava tradition.

Simhasanadhipathi.description: A title meaning 'occupant of the lion throne,' given to the seventy-four Vaishnava acharyas established by Ramanuja.

retinue.description: A group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

parasol.description: A ceremonial umbrella, often used as a symbol of royalty or honor in South Indian tradition.

thambi.description: A Tamil term meaning 'younger brother,' often used as a friendly or affectionate form of address.

Nambi.description: A respectful Tamil term for a pious or learned man, often used as a nickname for Azhwarkkadiyan.

Nambigaḷe.description: A respectful form of address in Tamil, meaning 'O revered one' or 'sir.'

pasurams.description: Devotional hymns composed by the Tamil Alwars, especially those in praise of Vishnu.

Tamil Veda.description: A term for the Divya Prabandham, the collection of hymns by the Alwars, considered the Tamil equivalent of the Sanskrit Vedas.

acharya.description: A spiritual preceptor or teacher, especially in the Vaishnava tradition.

divine plays.description: Religious dramas or enactments of stories from Hindu mythology, performed during temple festivals.

Sengannan Sambuvaraiyar.description: A powerful clan-chief of Chola Nadu and lord of Kadambur Palace; he is Kandhamaaran's father and a notable figure in the Chola court.

Pazhuvetaraiyar.description: A senior noble and military commander, renowned for his valor and battle scars; he is the chief guest at the Kadambur gathering and a key figure in the Chola kingdom.

Maara Vel.description: Another name for Kandhamaaran, used by his family; he is the son of Sambuvarayar.

Sambuvaraiyar Palace.description: The grand residence of Sengannan Sambuvaraiyar in Kadambur, serving as a political and social hub.

Vanagapadi.description: A region or territory in the Chola kingdom, identified as Vandiyathevan's home area.

Thiruvallam.description: A village or town in Vanagapadi, cited as Vandiyathevan's native place.

Pennai.description: A river in southern India, marking the northern boundary where Vandiyathevan and Kandhamaaran once served as border guards.

Kanyakumari.description: The southernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent, used here to denote the southern extent of Chola fame.

Mazhavarayar.description: Another noble family or chieftaincy in the Chola realm, mentioned as someone Vandiyathevan wished to meet.

Vanar.description: The clan or dynasty to which Vandiyathevan belongs, historically associated with the region around Thiruvallam.

Periya Pazhuvetaraiyar.description: A title meaning 'Elder Pazhuvetaraiyar,' referring to the most senior member of the Pazhuvetaraiyar family.

naazhigai.description: A traditional Tamil unit of time, roughly equivalent to 24 minutes.

scabbard.description: A sheath for holding a sword.

signet ring.description: A ring bearing an official seal, used to authenticate documents or as a mark of authority.

insignia.description: A badge or emblem signifying rank or authority.

citadel.description: A fortress protecting a town, often at its highest point.

ramparts.description: Defensive walls or embankments surrounding a fort or palace.

minions of Yama.description: A figurative phrase referring to the servants of Yama, the Hindu god of death, implying fearsome guards.

Subramanya.description: A Hindu deity, also known as Murugan or Kartikeya, god of war and victory.

Surapadman.description: A demon in Hindu mythology, famously slain by Lord Subramanya.

kumkum.description: A red powder used for religious and social markings in Hindu culture, though not directly in this passage, it is commonly referenced in similar settings.

Kandanmaran.description: A nobleman and friend of Vandiyathevan, Kandanmaran is the son of the lord of Kadambur and plays host to Vandiyathevan at Kadambur Palace.

Devaralan.description: A male ritual dancer who performs the Velan dance, believed to be possessed by the god Murugan during the trance.

Devaratti.description: A female ritual dancer who partners with Devaralan in the Velan dance, enacting mythological stories on stage.

Kadambur Palace.description: A grand palace belonging to Kandanmaran's family, serving as the setting for the chapter's events and gatherings.

Tamil Nadu.description: A region in southern India, historically the heartland of the Chola dynasty.

Chera.description: An ancient South Indian dynasty and region, often in rivalry or alliance with the Cholas.

Veeranarayana Puram.description: A town or locality mentioned as a place where Vandiyathevan witnessed Pazhuvettaraiyar's entourage.

Sinhalese.description: Refers to people from Sri Lanka (ancient Ceylon), indicating possible origins of Pazhuvettaraiyar's wife.

Kashmir.description: A region in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, mentioned as a possible homeland of the mysterious woman.

Java.description: An island in present-day Indonesia, referenced as a distant foreign land.

Kadaram.description: An ancient name for Kedah, a region in present-day Malaysia, known for its historical links with South India.

Yavana.description: A term used in ancient India to refer to Greeks or Western foreigners.

Misra.description: The Tamil name for Egypt, used here to suggest exotic foreign origins.

Arabia.description: The Arabian Peninsula, referenced as a land where women traditionally wear veils.

Kuravai.description: A traditional Tamil folk dance performed by women, often as part of temple festivals and rituals.

Murugan.description: A popular Tamil deity, also known as Kartikeya or Skanda, god of war and victory.

Gajamukha.description: A demon with the face of an elephant, another adversary of Murugan in mythology.

Velavan.description: An epithet of Murugan, meaning 'the one who wields the vel (spear)'.

Velan dance.description: A ritual dance dedicated to Murugan, involving trance and enactment of mythological stories.

Vel.description: The sacred spear associated with Murugan, symbolizing divine power and victory.

Durga.description: A fierce Hindu goddess, worshipped as a protector and slayer of demons.

Bhadrakali.description: A form of the goddess Kali, associated with protection and destruction of evil.

Chandikeswari.description: A fierce goddess, worshipped for her role in slaying the demon Mahishasura.

Sooran.description: Another name for Surapadman, the demon king defeated by Murugan.

asura.description: A class of powerful demons or anti-gods in Hindu mythology.

entourage.description: A group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

parasols.description: Large decorative umbrellas used as symbols of royalty or status.

battlements.description: The defensive, notched parapets at the top of a fort or palace wall.

kanne.description: A type of flower considered sacred and used in traditional Tamil garlands.

kanthal.description: A flower native to Tamil regions, significant in local culture and rituals.

kurinji.description: A rare blue flower that blooms in the hills of Tamil Nadu every twelve years, symbolizing love and beauty.

sevvalari.description: A red flower associated with Murugan and used in ritual garlands.

kunri beads.description: Bright red seeds of the Abrus precatorius plant, used in traditional jewelry and decorations.

areca nut.description: The seed of the areca palm, chewed with betel leaves as a traditional practice.

kovai fruit.description: A small red fruit (ivy gourd) whose color is used metaphorically to describe redness, especially of eyes.

udukkai.description: A small, hourglass-shaped drum used in South Indian music and temple rituals.

pullanguzhal.description: A traditional Tamil flute used in folk and classical music.

parai.description: A large, flat drum played with sticks, used in Tamil folk and ritual music.

karadi.description: A barrel-shaped drum used in Tamil folk music.

Vallavarayan.description: A young nobleman and the protagonist of the story, also known as Vandiyathevan, who serves as a messenger and adventurer in the Chola Empire.

Kandhamaran.description: Vallavarayan's close friend, the son of Sambuvarayar, and an important nobleman involved in the political intrigues of the Chola court.

Sambuvaraiyars.description: A prominent chieftain family allied with the Chola dynasty, with Sambuvarayar being the head of the house.

Perunilakizhar.description: A dignitary from Kunrathur, recognized as a minor king or noble.

Pallavarayar.description: A noble associated with the legacy of the Pallavas, referred to as 'of the Three Crowns.'

Kalingarayar.description: A minor king, referred to as 'Dangling Kalingarayar,' possibly indicating his region or a nickname.

Vanangamudi Munaiyarayar.description: A chieftain or noble present at the midnight assembly.

Devasenathipathi Poovarayar.description: A dignitary with a military title (commander of the divine army), present at the gathering.

Singamutharaiyar.description: Known as the 'Fearless,' a minor king or chieftain at the assembly.

Rajaliyar.description: Referred to as 'Twin-Parasol Rajaliyar,' indicating status and authority among the minor kings.

Perunila Velar.description: A noble from Kollimalai, present among the dignitaries.

Sundara Chola Chakravarthi.description: The reigning emperor of the Chola Empire, ruling from Pazhayarai.

Azhwarkadiyan Nambi.description: A mysterious and cunning Vaishnavite spy, known for his wit and involvement in secretive affairs.

Mathanda Nayakar.description: The northern lord whom Vandiyathevan serves; a powerful noble in the Chola Empire.

kuravai.description: A traditional Tamil folk dance, often performed during festivals and celebrations.

Mazhapadi.description: A region or town under the rule of Mazhavarayar.

Kunrathur.description: A town or region represented by Perunilakizhar.

Three Crowns.description: A term referring to the three ancient Tamil kingdoms: Chola, Chera, and Pandya.

Devasenathipathi.description: A title meaning 'commander of the divine army.'

Poovarayar.description: A noble or chieftain, possibly from a region named Poovara.

Kollimalai.description: A hill region in Tamil Nadu, under the rule of Perunila Velar.

Chola Empire.description: The dominant South Indian dynasty during the 10th century, known for its military and cultural achievements.

Pazhayarai.description: A major city and royal seat of the Chola dynasty.

Kali temple.description: A temple dedicated to the goddess Kali, known for her fierce and protective aspects.

Kali.description: A Hindu goddess associated with destruction and transformation.

Vaidhumba kings.description: A royal dynasty that once ruled over the Vanar clan's territory.

Vanar clan.description: An ancient royal lineage to which Vallavarayan belongs.

Arai­yar.description: A title of respect and authority, evolved from 'Raja' or 'King,' used for minor kings and nobles.

vimana.description: The tower or spire above the sanctum of a South Indian temple.

Chakravarthi.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'emperor' or 'universal ruler.'

Sambuvaraiyar.description: A chieftain and lord of the Sambuvaraya clan, Sambuvaraiyar is a prominent nobleman and a participant in the political machinations surrounding the Chola succession.

Sembiyan Mahadevi.description: The revered dowager queen and mother of Sundara Chola, Sembiyan Mahadevi is known for her piety, wisdom, and influence in royal decisions.

Kundavai Devi.description: The intelligent and politically astute daughter of Sundara Chola, Kundavai Devi is respected for her counsel and plays a significant role in the Chola court.

Arulmozhi Varman.description: The younger son of Sundara Chola, also known as Raja Raja Chola I, Arulmozhi Varman is the commander of the southern forces and beloved by the people.

Chinna Pazhuvettarayar.description: The younger brother of Pazhuvettaraiyar, Chinna Pazhuvettarayar is the guardian of Tanjore Fort and an influential figure in court politics.

Malavaraiyar.description: A nobleman and chieftain, Malavaraiyar is one of the assembled lords participating in the discussion about the Chola succession.

Thiruppurambiyam.description: A historic battlefield where a decisive victory helped establish Chola supremacy.

Velur.description: A location associated with a significant battle in Chola history.

Thakkolam.description: A battlefield where the Cholas fought and lost many warriors.

Eezham.description: The Tamil name for Sri Lanka, often referenced in the context of Chola military campaigns.

Dasaratha.description: A legendary king from the Ramayana, father of Rama, cited here as a model of royal deliberation.

Rama.description: A revered prince and hero of the Ramayana, often invoked as an ideal ruler.

Pazhuvur Mahārāja.description: A title referring to the chief of Pazhuvur, namely Pazhuvettaraiyar.

Mutharaiyars.description: A powerful dynasty and rivals of the early Cholas, defeated by Vijayalaya Chola.

Madurai Pandyas.description: A prominent South Indian dynasty and rivals of the Cholas, based in Madurai.

Karikala Valavan.description: A legendary early Chola king famed for his engineering feats, especially the banks of the Kaveri river.

Tungabhadra.description: A river in southern India, marking the northern extent of Chola influence.

Pandya Nadu.description: The land ruled by the Pandya dynasty, in southern Tamil Nadu.

Nanjil Nadu.description: A fertile region in southern Tamil Nadu, part of the Chola empire.

Thondai Mandalam.description: A region in northern Tamil Nadu, historically significant in Chola times.

Pāgi Nadu.description: A territorial division or region under Chola control.

Gangapadi.description: A region in present-day Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, conquered by the Cholas.

Nulambapadi.description: A region under Chola rule, likely in present-day Karnataka.

Vaithumba Nadu.description: A territorial division or region mentioned as part of the Chola empire.

Chitpuli Nadu.description: A region or administrative division within the Chola empire.

Perumpanappadi.description: A large territorial division under the Cholas.

Kodagu.description: A region in present-day Karnataka, known as the birthplace of the river Kaveri.

Vengi.description: A region in present-day Andhra Pradesh, contested by the Cholas.

Kanchipuram.description: A historic city in Tamil Nadu, seat of the northern Chola army and site of the golden palace.

Parantaka Chakravarthi.description: A celebrated Chola emperor, known for his conquests and piety.

Kudagu.description: Another form of Kodagu, the region where the Kaveri river originates.

Thanjai.description: An alternate name for Thanjavur, the Chola capital.

Kudamurutti.description: A branch of the Kaveri river in Tamil Nadu.

Alli Rani.description: A legendary queen in Tamil folklore, symbolizing a matriarchal or woman-ruled kingdom.

Maharaja.description: A Sanskrit title meaning 'great king' or emperor.

soothsayer.description: A person who claims to foretell events or predict the future, often consulted in royal courts.

dharma.description: A Sanskrit term meaning duty, moral law, or righteous conduct, especially in the context of war or governance.

Nadu.description: A Tamil term for 'land' or 'country,' often used to denote administrative regions.

padi.description: A suffix in Tamil denoting a region or division of land.

Devi.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'goddess' or a respectful title for a noblewoman or princess.

Vanangamudiyar.description: A respected nobleman and warrior, Vanangamudiyar is known for his candor and loyalty, participating in the secret council.

Sundara Chola Maharaja.description: The reigning emperor of the Chola dynasty, Sundara Chola is elderly and ailing, prompting debates over the succession.

Kandaraditya Devar.description: A former Chola king, remembered for his virtue and wisdom; father of Madurantaka and husband of Chembiyan Mahadevi.

Madurantaka Devar.description: Son of Kandaraditya Devar, Madurantaka is a prince whose claim to the throne is being debated; known for his earlier devotion to asceticism.

Arinjaya Devar.description: Younger brother of Kandaraditya Devar, who briefly ruled as Chola king after his brother's death.

Parantaka Sundara Chola.description: Also called Sundara Chola Maharaja, he is Arinjaya Devar's son and the current emperor.

Chembiyan Mahadevi.description: The chief queen and dharmapatni of Kandaraditya Devar, known for her piety and influence in the royal family.

Sembiyan Madevi.description: Mother of Madurantaka Devar, also known as Chembiyan Mahadevi, she is revered for her devotion and is influential in her son's decisions.

Kali Yuga.description: The current age in Hindu cosmology, considered an era of decline and moral decay.

Arinjaya Chola.description: A Chola king who ruled briefly after Kandaraditya's death.

Manu.description: Refers to the ancient lawgiver in Hindu tradition, whose laws (Manusmriti) are considered authoritative on matters of dharma and succession.

Durga Devi.description: A powerful Hindu goddess, invoked here as a divine witness for oaths and pledges.

Shaiva.description: Pertaining to Shaivism, a major tradition of Hinduism devoted to the worship of Shiva.

Periya Piratti.description: A respectful term meaning 'great lady' or 'chief queen', here referring to Sembiyan Madevi.

Manmatha.description: The Hindu god of love, known for his beauty; used as a metaphor for a handsome prince.

bangle.description: A rigid bracelet, typically made of metal, wood, or glass, worn around the wrist, common in South Asian cultures.

armlet.description: An ornamental band worn around the upper arm, often signifying royalty or high status.

nazhikai.description: A traditional Tamil unit of time, roughly equivalent to 24 minutes.

dharmapatni.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'lawful wife', especially one who upholds dharma (righteousness) in the household.

Devar.description: A Tamil honorific meaning 'lord' or 'divine one', used for royalty or respected nobles.

Thevar.description: A variant of 'Devar', also meaning 'lord' or 'chieftain'.

Piratti.description: A Tamil term for 'lady' or 'queen', used as a respectful title for royal women.

Madurantakan.description: Son of Kandaradithar and a devout Shaivite, Madurantakan is a claimant to the Chola throne, supported by powerful factions within the empire.

Manimekalai.description: Kandhamaran's shy and modest sister, whose marriage becomes a point of political alliance.

Kandaradithar.description: A former Chola king and father of Madurantakan, remembered for his piety and devotion to Shiva.

Palar.description: A river in southern India, marking the northern boundary of the Chola heartland.

Chanakya.description: An ancient Indian statesman and strategist, often referenced as a symbol of political wisdom and cunning.

Thondai.description: A historical region in northern Tamil Nadu, significant as a battleground for Chola expansion.

Madurantaka.description: A claimant to the Chola throne, supported by the Pazhuvettaraiyars.

Shaivites.description: Followers of Shaivism, a major sect of Hinduism devoted to the worship of Shiva.

watch.description: A division of the night or day used in traditional timekeeping, often referring to a period of about three hours.

Kumbhakarna’s service.description: A humorous reference to sleeping deeply, likening it to the legendary giant Kumbhakarna from the Ramayana, known for his long slumbers.

Vanathi.description: A noblewoman from the Kodumbalur clan and companion to Kundavai; she is depicted as modest, sweet, and serene, and is destined for a significant role in the story.

Rajendra.description: Son of Rajaraja, raised by Kundavai to become a renowned warrior and king.

Astrologer.description: The astrologer of Kudanthai, a respected figure whom Kundavai and Vanathi visit to inquire about Vanathi’s future.

Meenalocani.description: One of the radiant women in the boat, named among the companions of the Ponni river.

Neelalocani.description: Another of the radiant women in the boat, also a companion of the Ponni river.

Lord of the Ocean.description: A poetic reference to the sea, depicted as the bridegroom of the river Ponni.

punna.description: A type of tree (Calophyllum inophyllum) with fragrant flowers, common in South India.

Arisilaaru.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, described as a hidden and beautiful tributary of the Kaveri.

veena.description: A traditional South Indian stringed musical instrument.

Silappathikaram.description: An ancient Tamil epic, from which the verses sung by the maidens are taken.

Avvaiyar.description: A legendary Tamil poetess and saint, celebrated for her wisdom and chastity.

Kudanthai.description: The Tamil name for the town of Kumbakonam, where the astrologer resides.

Ambika.description: A form of the Hindu goddess Parvati, depicted in a painting in the astrologer's house.

Saraswati.description: The Hindu goddess of knowledge, music, and arts.

Lakshmi.description: The Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity.

Chozhar.description: A Tamil term for Chola, referring to the Chola dynasty.

Ambikai.description: Another form of the goddess Parvati, worshipped in South India.

Jyotishar.description: A term for astrologer in Tamil/Sanskrit.

Parashakti.description: A supreme form of the Hindu goddess, representing ultimate power.

Kodumbalur.description: A noble clan and region in Tamil Nadu, to which Vanathi belongs.

arugam.description: A type of sacred grass (Eragrostis cynosuroides) used in Hindu rituals and garlands.

kumudam.description: A white water lily or lotus, symbolizing purity and beauty in Indian literature.

koel.description: A type of cuckoo bird known for its melodious call, often referenced in Indian poetry.

Indrani.description: The queen of the gods in Hindu mythology, consort of Indra.

chariot.description: A horse-drawn vehicle used for transport, especially by royalty and nobility in ancient India.

Akka.description: A Tamil word meaning 'elder sister', used as a respectful form of address.

horoscope.description: An astrological chart or diagram representing the positions of planets and stars at the time of a person's birth, used to predict their future.

mantra.description: A sacred utterance, sound, or phrase in Hinduism believed to have spiritual power.

palm-leaf manuscripts.description: Ancient documents written on dried palm leaves, commonly used in South India for recording texts.

Kumbakonam.description: A city in Tamil Nadu, South India, known for its temples and religious significance; called Kudanthai in the Chola period.

Kudamooku.description: An alternative historical name for Kumbakonam/Kudanthai.

Amma.description: A Tamil term of respect and endearment for women, meaning 'mother' or 'lady.'

Maha Vishnu.description: A principal deity in Hinduism, regarded as the preserver and protector of the universe.

Jayalakshmi.description: The Hindu goddess of wealth and fortune, also known as Lakshmi.

Kailasa.description: The mythical abode of Lord Shiva in Hindu tradition, symbolizing the ultimate spiritual realm.

Pushpaka Vimana.description: A mythical flying chariot from Hindu epics, symbolizing divine or magical transport.

Asalur.description: A place mentioned as the possible origin of Vandiyathevan by the astrologer.

Arisil.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, near which the chariot waits for the princesses.

Brihaspati.description: The Hindu god of wisdom and the planet Jupiter, symbolizing intelligence and learning.

Arjuna.description: A legendary hero and warrior prince from the Mahabharata, symbolizing valor and strength.

penance.description: A religious or spiritual practice involving self-discipline or austerity, often to seek blessings or forgiveness.

lotus feet.description: A poetic expression in Indian literature referring to the feet of a revered person, likened to the beauty and purity of a lotus flower.

prasadam.description: A religious offering, usually food or sacred items, distributed to devotees after being blessed.

charioteer.description: A person who drives a chariot.

disciple.description: A student or follower, especially of a religious or learned person.

banyan leaf.description: A large leaf from the banyan tree, often symbolically significant in Indian culture.

tiger flag.description: A symbol of the Chola dynasty, whose royal emblem was the tiger.

Nandini.description: The beautiful and enigmatic young wife of Pazhuvettaraiyar, central to many of the novel's intrigues.

Veerapandiyan.description: The defeated Pandya king, brought to Nandini's house after a great battle with the Cholas.

Nambi Adigal.description: A respectful title for a devout Vaishnavite, here referring to Azhwarkkadiyan.

Panchakshara mantra.description: The sacred five-syllable mantra 'Namashivaya', central to Shaivite worship.

Namashivaya.description: The five-syllable mantra dedicated to Lord Shiva, considered highly sacred by Shaivites.

Perumal.description: Another Tamil name for Lord Vishnu, especially in the context of temple worship.

Srirangam.description: A sacred island town in Tamil Nadu, home to the famous Ranganathaswamy temple dedicated to Vishnu.

Thiruvanaikka.description: A holy town near Srirangam, famous for its Jambukeswarar temple dedicated to Shiva.

Vaishnavan.description: A devotee of Lord Vishnu, representing the Vaishnavite sect.

Tripura.description: Refers to the mythological three cities destroyed by Shiva, symbolizing a key Shaivite legend.

Veera Narayanapuram.description: A place referenced in the story, likely associated with religious debates or events.

Alwars.description: The twelve poet-saints devoted to Vishnu, whose hymns helped spread Vaishnavism.

Nayanmars.description: The sixty-three poet-saints devoted to Shiva, central to the spread of Saivism.

Kerala.description: A region to the west of Tamil Nadu, mentioned as the birthplace of a great sage.

Kaladi.description: A village in Kerala, famed as the birthplace of Adi Shankara.

Advaita Vedanta.description: A non-dualistic school of Hindu philosophy established by Adi Shankara.

Bharat.description: The traditional Sanskrit name for India.

Pandya.description: A historic South Indian dynasty, rivals to the Cholas.

Vaigai River.description: A river in southern Tamil Nadu, flowing through Madurai and Pandya country.

Thiruppanandal.description: A town near the Kollidam river, mentioned as a place to procure a horse.

Azhwars.description: Alternate spelling of Alwars, the Vaishnavite poet-saints.

Thiruvengadam.description: The sacred hill now known as Tirupati, a major pilgrimage site for Vaishnavites.

Iranyasuran.description: A mythological demon king, here used as an epithet for Pazhuvettaraiyar.

Nambigal.description: A respectful term for a religious person, especially a Vaishnavite.

sannyasi.description: A Hindu ascetic who has renounced worldly life.

gopuram.description: A monumental tower at the entrance of a South Indian temple.

Velanattam.description: A ritual dance performed by a Velan (male priest) and Velatti (female priestess) in Tamil folk tradition.

sannadham.description: A formal proclamation or announcement, often made during temple rituals.

tulsi.description: Holy basil, a sacred plant in Hinduism, often used in worship and garlands.

Kudanthai astrologer.description: A renowned astrologer based in Kudanthai (Kumbakonam), known for his wisdom and cryptic speech, who provides guidance and predictions to various characters.

Alwarkadiyan Nambi.description: A mysterious and devout Vaishnavite spy, also known as Thirumalaiyappan, who appears in various disguises and gathers intelligence for his own purposes.

Chinna Pazhuvettaraiyar.description: The younger Pazhuvettaraiyar brother, also a high-ranking official and commander, closely allied with his elder brother.

Kundavai Piratti.description: A respectful title for Princess Kundavai, denoting her royal status.

Mahaarajya.description: A term meaning 'great kingdom' or 'empire', used here to refer to the Chola Empire.

Ani.description: A month in the Tamil calendar, corresponding roughly to June-July.

Purattasi.description: A month in the Tamil calendar, corresponding roughly to September-October.

Karthigai.description: A month in the Tamil calendar, corresponding roughly to November-December.

Margazhi.description: A month in the Tamil calendar, corresponding roughly to December-January.

Saptarishis.description: A constellation known as the 'Seven Sages' in Indian astronomy, identified with the Big Dipper.

Advaitins.description: Followers of Advaita Vedanta, a non-dualistic school of Hindu philosophy.

Padmini.description: One of the four traditional types of women described in Indian physiognomy, symbolizing lotus-like qualities.

Chithini.description: One of the four types of women in Indian physiognomy.

Gandharvi.description: One of the four types of women in Indian physiognomy, associated with musical or celestial qualities.

Vidyadhari.description: One of the four types of women in Indian physiognomy, associated with supernatural or magical qualities.

dais.description: A raised platform or seat of honor, typically used by people of status.

Jyotidar.description: A term for an astrologer or one who practices astrology.

veshti.description: A traditional South Indian garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs, worn by men.

Chakravarti.description: A Sanskrit term for a universal emperor or sovereign ruler.

Thiruvaiyaru.description: A town near Thanjavur, famous for its temples and as a crossing point over the rivers in the Chola region.

Vettaru.description: Another river or distributary in the Chola heartland, crossed by travelers.

Vennaru.description: A river in the Chola region, one of the distributaries of the Kaveri.

tank.description: A man-made reservoir or pond used for irrigation and water storage in South Indian villages.

sengazhuneer.description: A type of aquatic flower, also known as the red water-lily, native to South India.

choli.description: A traditional game played by girls in South India, involving small objects or stones.

pallanguzhi.description: A traditional South Indian board game played with seeds or shells in pits on a wooden board.

kokkarakko.description: Onomatopoeic Tamil word for the clucking sound made by chickens.

karagam.description: A decorated pot balanced on the head during folk dances and religious processions in Tamil Nadu.

udukku.description: A small hourglass-shaped drum played with the hands, used in South Indian folk and temple music.

nagara.description: A large drum used in temple rituals and processions in South India.

Ayyo.description: An exclamation in Tamil expressing surprise, alarm, or distress.

Tharagai.description: One of the young women attending Kundavai Devi, known for her outspoken and sometimes teasing nature.

Varini.description: Another attendant in Kundavai Devi's circle, often critical of Vanathi and quick to express jealousy.

Niravathi.description: A companion of Kundavai Devi, who often joins in the gossip and speculation about Vanathi.

Sendhru.description: One of the young women in the princess's retinue, participating in the banter and gossip.

Mandakini.description: A member of Kundavai Devi's group, who offers explanations and insights during the conversation.

Maniya Keda.description: A kingdom mentioned as one of the realms whose rulers wish to form alliances with the Chola prince through marriage.

Kannosi.description: A distant northern kingdom, referenced as one of the many seeking alliance with the Cholas.

astrologer.description: A person who practices astrology, consulted in traditional Indian society for advice on auspicious times and causes of maladies.

magic powder.description: A reference to a supposed mystical or magical substance used in folk beliefs to enchant or influence someone.

maiden.description: An archaic term for an unmarried young woman.

swoon.description: An old-fashioned word for fainting, often used in the context of overwhelming emotion.

plank.description: A flat piece of timber, here used as a part of the boat's structure.

crocodile doll.description: A lifelike model or effigy of a crocodile, used here as part of a psychological ruse.

Rajakesari Varman Parantaka Sundara Choz.description: The reigning emperor of the Chola dynasty at the time of the story, known for his noble qualities and military campaigns.

Sundara Chozha.description: Another name for Rajakesari Varman Parantaka Sundara Chozha, the central emperor in this period, renowned for his beauty and leadership.

Arinjaya.description: Brother of Kandaradithar and father of Sundara Chozha, who ruled briefly before his death.

Paranthakan.description: A Chola commander from the Kodumbalur chieftain family, known as Chinna Velan, who died heroically in battle in Lanka.

Kalyani.description: A princess of the Vaithumba royal line, mother of Sundara Chozha.

Chembiyan Maadevi.description: A respected elder queen in the Chola palace at Pazhayarai, whom noblewomen serve.

Chozha.description: A powerful South Indian dynasty that ruled large parts of southern India and beyond during the medieval period.

Chozha empire.description: The territory ruled by the Chozha dynasty, noted for its military strength and cultural achievements.

Aattrur.description: A place in the land of Thondai where Arinjaya passed away.

Sevur.description: The site of a significant battle between the Chozha and Pandya armies.

King Mahindan.description: The king of Lanka who aided the Pandyas against the Chozhas.

Chinna Velan.description: A title meaning 'Young Velan', used for Paranthakan of Kodumbalur.

Sena.description: The general of King Mahinda of Lanka.

Eelathu Patta Paranthakan Chinna Velan.description: An honorific meaning 'Paranthakan Chinna Velan, who fell in Lanka', commemorating his heroic death.

Rashtrakutas.description: A powerful dynasty from the Deccan region, adversaries of the Chozhas in the north.

Vaithumba.description: A royal lineage, once adversaries of the Chola dynasty, to which Kalyani belonged.

Arulmozhi Thevar.description: A respectful title for Arulmozhi Varman, with 'Thevar' denoting nobility.

Velar.description: A title for chieftains or nobility, especially those from Kodumbalur.

aarthi.description: A Hindu ritual of waving lighted lamps before a deity or person as a mark of respect and to ward off evil.

sacred ash.description: Vibhuti, holy ash applied to the forehead as a religious mark in Shaivism.

anointed.description: To smear or apply a substance (like sacred ash or oil) ceremonially, often for blessings or protection.

warded off evil.description: A ritual act performed to protect someone from bad luck or negative influences, often involving gestures or substances like ash or turmeric.

akka.description: A Tamil word meaning 'elder sister', used as a term of respect and affection.

Arisil river.description: A river in the Chola region, serving as a scenic backdrop for events in the story.

conch.description: A large seashell used as a wind instrument in Hindu rituals and ceremonies.

plantain fiber.description: Fiber derived from the stem of the banana plant, commonly used for making ropes or stuffing.

Thirumalaiyappan.description: Also known as Azhwarkadiyan Nambi, he is a clever and resourceful Vaishnavite spy who plays a key role in uncovering conspiracies in the Chola kingdom.

Idumbankari.description: A servant from Kadambur, he is involved in secretive activities and is seen acting suspiciously in this chapter.

Soman Sambavan.description: A mysterious man who meets Idumbankari by the riverbank, appearing to be involved in clandestine plans.

peepal tree.description: A sacred fig tree (Ficus religiosa) revered in Indian tradition and often found near temples and riverbanks.

Bharatanatyam.description: A classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, known for its expressive gestures and mudras.

shastra.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'treatise' or 'scripture,' often referring to authoritative texts on arts or sciences.

mudra.description: A symbolic hand gesture used in Indian classical dance and religious rituals.

Matsyavataram.description: The fish incarnation, the first avatar of Vishnu in Hindu mythology.

Veera Saiva.description: A term referring to a staunch or heroic follower of Shaivism.

kudumi.description: A traditional tuft of hair worn by Hindu men, especially Brahmins, on the crown of the head.

Pullirukkum Vellur.description: A place name, possibly a village or town, referenced as the home of the Veera Saiva.

ashoka tree.description: A sacred flowering tree (Saraca asoca) often associated with Indian mythology and temple grounds.

Machahasta mudra.description: A specific hand gesture in Indian dance symbolizing a fish.

Prithiveepathi.description: A king of the Ganga dynasty, historically associated with the region and its military barracks.

Manniyaru.description: A river mentioned as part of the landscape, possibly a tributary or local waterway.

ghat.description: A series of steps leading down to a river, often used for bathing or religious rituals.

Appane.description: A Tamil term of address, meaning 'sir,' 'father,' or 'dear one,' used respectfully.

Aditya Chola.description: Son of Vijayalaya Chola, a great warrior who fought alongside the Pallavas at Thiruppurambiyam.

Varaguna Varman.description: The Pandya king during the period of the Battle of Thiruppurambiyam, adversary to the Pallavas and Cholas.

Aparajita Varman.description: The Pallava king who fought against the Pandyas at Thiruppurambiyam, aided by the Cholas and Gangas.

Ravidasan.description: A conspirator involved in plotting against the Chola kingdom, present at the secret meeting near the ruined temple.

Nadukal Temple.description: A memorial stone temple erected in honor of fallen warriors in Tamil tradition.

Pallippadai.description: A temple built over the burial site of a king or noble, often with a consecrated idol.

Ganga king.description: Refers to the rulers of the Ganga dynasty, allies of the Pallavas during the battle.

Perunarkilli.description: An ancient Chola king celebrated in Tamil literature.

Ilanchetchenni.description: An early Chola king, part of the dynasty's illustrious lineage.

Thodithot Sembiyan.description: A Chola king, remembered for his rule and contributions to the dynasty.

Pallavas.description: A major dynasty in northern Tamil Nadu, often in conflict with the Pandyas and Cholas.

Kozhi Vendhar.description: A title meaning 'Kings of the Cock,' used by Chola rulers.

Chola kings.description: Rulers of the Chola dynasty, one of the most powerful South Indian empires.

Chola land.description: The territory ruled by the Chola dynasty.

Pandya king.description: The ruler of the Pandya dynasty.

Ganga country.description: The region ruled by the Ganga dynasty, allies of the Pallavas.

Keezhainaattu.description: A region or group of warriors in the Chola country.

Maravars.description: A martial community from southern Tamil Nadu, often serving as warriors.

Lord Vishnu.description: A major Hindu deity, often associated with protection and valor.

Devi Jayalakshmi.description: A Hindu goddess associated with fortune and grace.

mandapam.description: A pillared hall or pavilion, often part of a temple complex.

Machahasta.description: A group or faction involved in conspiracy, mentioned as 'Machahasta conspirators.'

hero stone.description: A memorial stone erected in honor of a fallen warrior.

idol.description: A sculpted image of a deity used for worship.

consecrated.description: Formally dedicated or made sacred, especially in a religious context.

shrine.description: A sacred place dedicated to a deity or revered figure.

lances.description: Long spears used by cavalry in battle.

discus.description: A circular weapon, here referring to the Sudarshana Chakra of Lord Vishnu.

core warriors.description: The most trusted and skilled fighters in an army.

war elephant.description: An elephant trained and used in battle.

Chola nation.description: Refers to the Chola kingdom or its people.

Chola kingdom.description: The territory ruled by the Chola dynasty.

Alwarkadiyan.description: A clever and resourceful Vaishnavite spy, also known as Thirumalaiyappan or Azhwarkkadiyan, who gathers intelligence for the Chola court.

Vanangamudimudiyaraiyar.description: A Chola noble and one of the dignitaries present at the Samburayar palace gathering.

Mazhapadi Mazhuvaraiyar.description: A Chola nobleman and one of the attendees at the palace council.

Sembiyan Devi.description: A senior Chola queen, known for her Shaivite devotion and temple renovations, suspected by conspirators of political cunning.

Pandya country.description: The territory ruled by the Pandya dynasty, rivals to the Cholas in southern India.

Mahodaya.description: A place near the Lankan coast, mentioned as a landing point from India.

palmyra tree.description: A tall palm tree common in South India and Sri Lanka, symbolically important and featured on coins.

oracle.description: A person through whom a deity is believed to speak, often during ritual dances.

Ayyarappar.description: The presiding deity (Shiva) of the main temple in Thiruvaiyaru.

choultry.description: A public rest house or inn, often used by travelers and pilgrims in South India.

yaazh.description: An ancient Tamil stringed musical instrument, similar to a harp.

kuzhal.description: A traditional South Indian wind instrument, akin to a flute or oboe.

muzhavu.description: A percussion instrument, a type of drum used in temple and classical music.

thannumai.description: A barrel-shaped drum used in traditional South Indian music.

Thirumalaiyappar.description: Another name for Azhwarkkadiyan, emphasizing his religious and philosophical background.
