Aippasi.description: A month in the Tamil calendar, roughly corresponding to mid-October to mid-November, associated with the northeast monsoon.

Thai.description: A Tamil month corresponding to mid-January to mid-February, marking the harvest season and favorable weather for sea travel.

Maasi.description: A Tamil month corresponding to mid-February to mid-March, also associated with favorable sea winds.

Vaikasi.description: A Tamil month corresponding to mid-May to mid-June, marking the onset of the Chozha wind.

Chozha wind.description: A seasonal wind named after the Chola dynasty, blowing during certain months and affecting sea travel between the Chola country and Lanka.

Kondal wind.description: A specific seasonal wind in the region, considered safe for sea travel during certain months.

Palani.description: A sacred hill temple in Tamil Nadu dedicated to Lord Murugan, invoked here as a deity for protection.

Parameswara.description: A name for Lord Shiva, one of the principal Hindu deities, invoked in prayer during moments of crisis.

Umapati.description: Another name for Lord Shiva, meaning 'consort of Uma (Parvati)', invoked for divine help.

waist-cloth.description: A traditional garment, usually a long piece of cloth tied around the waist, commonly worn by men in South India.

coir.description: A natural fiber extracted from the husk of coconuts, used for making ropes and mats.

raft.description: A flat structure, typically made of planks or logs, used as a floating platform or for support in water.

Samudrakumari.description: An epithet meaning 'Daughter of the Sea', used for Poonguzhali in the text.

Paranjothi.description: A Tamil term meaning 'Supreme Light', used here as a metaphor for divinity or the Sun God.

Sun God.description: A reference to Surya, the Hindu solar deity worshipped as the Sun.

Saptarishi.description: A prominent constellation (the Big Dipper/Ursa Major) in Indian astronomy, representing the seven great sages.

Arundhati.description: A star in the Saptarishi constellation, revered in Hindu tradition as the faithful wife of sage Vashishta.

Vashishta.description: One of the seven great sages (rishis) in Hindu mythology, represented as a star in the Saptarishi constellation.

Pole Star.description: Also known as Dhruva Nakshatra, a fixed star in the northern sky used for navigation.

Nagathivu.description: An island off the northern coast of Lanka (Sri Lanka), also known as Nainativu.

Pulastiyanagar.description: An ancient city in Lanka, traditionally associated with the sage Pulastya and identified with Polonnaruwa.

Ponni’s Son.description: A title for Arulmozhi Varman, meaning 'Son of the Ponni (Cauvery) River', signifying his connection to the Chola heartland.

Nagath Theevu.description: Another spelling for Nagathivu, an island near Lanka.

Boothath Theevu.description: An island near Nagath Theevu, known as the 'Island of Spirits', reputed to be haunted.

Bodhath Theevu.description: The ancient name for Boothath Theevu, associated with Lord Buddha's legendary visit to Lanka.

Lord Buddha.description: The founder of Buddhism, believed in some traditions to have visited Lanka.

Dharma.description: A key concept in Indian religions, meaning righteousness, moral law, or the teachings of the Buddha.

sanctum sanctorum.description: The innermost, most sacred chamber of a Hindu temple where the main deity is enshrined.

mat.description: A woven reed or grass sheet used for sitting or sleeping, here referring to a boat mat.

garment.description: A piece of clothing; in this context, refers to the cloth Vandiyathevan is wearing.

water gourd.description: A container made from a dried gourd, traditionally used in South India to carry water.

half-scroll.description: A partial or folded palm-leaf manuscript, used for writing letters in ancient times.

Boothaththivu.description: An island near Lanka, its name means 'Island of Ghosts' in Tamil; believed to be haunted or mysterious.

Nagaththivu.description: Another island near Lanka, its name means 'Island of Serpents' in Tamil.

Maathottam.description: A coastal town or port in northern Lanka, historically significant as a trading and meeting place.

Samudra Kumari.description: Literally 'Daughter of the Ocean' in Tamil, a title given to Poonguzhali for her connection to the sea.

Poonthurai.description: An island or coastal area near Kodikkarai, associated with Poonguzhali.

Chola Emperor.description: The reigning king of the Chola dynasty, father of Ponniyin Selvan.

Garuda.description: A mythical bird and mount of the Hindu god Vishnu, symbolizing power and speed.

Sundara Chola Parantaka.description: The reigning emperor of the Chola dynasty, also known as the Tribhuvana Emperor, under whom the story unfolds.

Sri Sankara Bhagavatpadachariyar.description: A reference to Adi Shankara, the revered philosopher and founder of Advaita Vedanta.

Adi Saivites.description: Devotees and priests belonging to the Shaivite tradition, worshippers of Lord Shiva.

Veera Saivites.description: A sect of fervent Shaivite devotees known for their zealous worship of Shiva.

Pattars.description: Priests, especially those serving in Shaivite temples, responsible for guiding pilgrims and conducting rituals.

tirtha.description: A sacred water body or pilgrimage spot, often associated with ritual bathing.

Rama Theertham.description: A holy tank in Rameswaram associated with Lord Rama.

Lakshmana Theertham.description: A sacred tank named after Lakshmana, Rama's brother.

Anjaneya Theertham.description: A holy tank named after Hanuman (Anjaneya), the monkey god and devotee of Rama.

Sugreeva Theertham.description: A sacred water tank named after Sugreeva, the monkey king from the Ramayana.

Brahmahatya.description: The sin of killing a Brahmin, considered a grave transgression in Hindu tradition.

kshetra.description: A sacred place or pilgrimage site, especially one with religious significance.

Thirukkurugur.description: The birthplace of Nammazhwar, now known as Alwarthirunagari in Tamil Nadu.

Anbil.description: A place name, indicating the ancestral village of Aniruddha Brahmarayar.

Satcharavai.description: A location or landmark near the Rameswaram temple, mentioned as a point of reference.

Maya-vadi.description: A follower of the philosophy that the world is an illusion (Maya), often associated with Advaita Vedanta.

Adiyarkkadiyan.description: A term meaning 'servant of the devotees,' often used by Vaishnavite ascetics.

Pattarmani.description: A respectful or formal address for a priest, especially in the Shaivite tradition.

Brahmadi Rajar.description: A title meaning 'Chief among Brahmins' or 'Brahmin king,' used for Aniruddha Brahmarayar.

front tuft.description: A lock of hair (kudumi) worn at the front of the head, signifying religious identity among some South Indian communities.

heretical marks.description: Religious symbols or marks on the body considered unorthodox or contrary by rival sects.

ascetic.description: A person who practices severe self-discipline and abstention from worldly pleasures, often for religious reasons.

sandal paste.description: A fragrant paste made from sandalwood, applied to the forehead as a religious mark.

mirage.description: An optical illusion, here used metaphorically to refer to the world as an illusion (Maya) in philosophical discourse.

pavilion.description: A temporary or open structure, often used for gatherings or rituals near temples.

palace guards.description: Soldiers assigned to protect royalty or high officials, such as the Chief Minister.

Mahindan.description: The King of Lanka, adversary to the Chola forces during their campaign in the island.

Veera Pandiyan.description: A former ruler of the Pandya dynasty, whose death is believed to have ended the Pandya royal line.

Nanadesa Tisai Ayirathu Aindhu Nooruvar.description: A prominent merchant guild, also known as the 'Five Hundred of a Thousand Directions', involved in overseas trade under the Chola Empire.

Manakkavaram.description: An island or coastal region referenced as a site of Chola naval victories over pirates.

Sriranganatha.description: A form of the Hindu god Vishnu, enshrined at the famous temple in Srirangam, invoked for divine blessings.

Terinja Kaikkola.description: A regiment of elite, handpicked warriors in the Chola army, originally from the Kaikkolar community.

Aga Parivara Padai.description: The Imperial Household Regiment of the Chola Empire, composed of specially selected soldiers.

Therinja Kaikkolar Padai.description: The Chosen Regiment of Handpicked Kaikkolar warriors, an elite unit in the Chola military.

Sundara Chola Therinja Kaikkolar.description: The title given to the chosen Kaikkolar regiment during Sundara Chola's reign.

asuras.description: Mythological demons or anti-gods in Hindu tradition, often depicted as adversaries of the gods.

Jambudvipa.description: An ancient term for the Indian subcontinent in classical Indian cosmology.

Rohana.description: A mountainous region in Sri Lanka, believed to be a hiding place for Pandya royal treasures.

Munnirpazhantheevu.description: An ancient island and part of a group of sixteen thousand isles, referenced in Chola conquest plans.

Kudamalai.description: A region or mountain referenced in the context of Chola conquests.

Kollam.description: A port city in Kerala, significant in medieval trade and Chola campaigns.

Kalingam.description: An ancient kingdom in eastern India, corresponding to present-day Odisha.

Irattapadi.description: A region or territory mentioned in the context of Chola expansion.

Chakkarakkottam.description: A region or administrative division referenced in Chola military plans.

Angam.description: A territory or region mentioned among the lands to be conquered.

Vangam.description: A region, possibly referring to Bengal, targeted in Chola expansion.

Kosalam.description: An ancient kingdom in northern India, referenced in the Chola conquests.

Vidhegam.description: A region or kingdom mentioned in the context of Chola campaigns.

Koorjaram.description: A territory or region listed among the Chola's future conquests.

Panchalam.description: An ancient kingdom, often identified with the region of Panchala in northern India.

Kodumbalur Velalars.description: A prominent land-owning and warrior community, influential in the Chola period.

Tribhuvana.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'lord of the three worlds', used as an imperial epithet.

palm leaves.description: Traditional writing material made from dried palm fronds, used for record-keeping in ancient India.

platter.description: A large, flat serving dish, often used for presenting offerings or gifts.

millet.description: A type of small-seeded grain commonly grown and consumed in South India.

pigeon peas.description: A type of legume widely used in South Indian cuisine, also known as 'toor dal'.

battalion.description: A large military unit, typically consisting of several hundred to a few thousand soldiers.

division.description: A major military unit or formation, usually consisting of several battalions.

regiment.description: A military unit, larger than a battalion, often composed of several battalions.

Kaikkolar.description: A community traditionally associated with weaving and, during the Chola period, with military service.

Velaalar.description: A land-owning agricultural community in Tamil society, sometimes referenced in contrast to warrior classes.

Mahamandiri.description: A high-ranking minister or chief counselor in a royal court.

Sri R.S.L. Lakshmana Chettiar.description: A notable figure who was involved in the renovation of the temple in Anbil and received the copper plates from the Vellalar.

Mahamahopadhyaya Swaminatha Iyer.description: A distinguished scholar who examined the Anbil copper plates and recognized their historical significance.

Sri T.A. Gopinatha Rao.description: A scholar specializing in stone inscriptions, to whom Swaminatha Iyer handed over the copper plates for further study.

Madhava Battar.description: The scribe who recorded the land grant and genealogy on the Anbil copper plates.

Anbil Ananthalwan Swamigal.description: The grandfather of Aniruddha Brahmarayar, renowned for his devotion to Sri Ranganatha.

Narayana Pattachari.description: The father of Aniruddha Brahmarayar, known for his devotional singing of the Alwars' hymns.

Iswara Pattar.description: A devoted priest at the Veera Narayana Perumal temple, recognized for his piety and emotional response to the Azhwar hymns.

Mahinda.description: The king of Lanka, whose army is defeated and who flees to Rohana during the Chola campaign.

Kandaraditya.description: Another Chola prince who passed away before Sundara Chola became king.

Lalgudi.description: A taluk (administrative division) in the Tiruchirapalli district of Tamil Nadu.

Tiruchirapalli.description: A major district and city in Tamil Nadu, also known as Trichy.

Premapuri.description: The Sanskrit translation of 'Anbil', meaning 'city of love'.

Vellalar.description: A land-owning agricultural caste in Tamil society.

Anbil copper plates.description: Historical copper plate inscriptions discovered in Anbil, detailing Chola genealogy and land grants.

Anaimangalam.description: A location where similar Chola copper plates were previously discovered.

Thiruvalangadu.description: Another site known for Chola copper plate inscriptions.

Srivaishnava.description: A tradition of Vaishnavism (worship of Vishnu) prominent in South India.

Shaiva Kalamukha.description: A Shaivite sect known for ascetic practices and distinctive marks.

Gurudeva.description: A respectful term for a revered teacher or spiritual guru.

Sriman Narayana.description: A divine name for Vishnu, central to Vaishnavite worship.

Sri Ranganatha.description: A form of Vishnu enshrined in the famous Srirangam temple.

Pattachariyar.description: A priestly title, often denoting a learned Brahmin or temple priest.

lingam.description: An aniconic representation of Shiva, worshipped in Shaivism.

Hari.description: A name for Vishnu, used in devotional contexts.

Narayana Murti.description: A form or idol of Vishnu.

Jains.description: Followers of Jainism, an ancient Indian religion.

Buddhists.description: Followers of Buddhism, a major world religion originating in India.

Mukannappa.description: A Tamil epithet for Shiva, meaning 'three-eyed lord'.

Vadavengadam.description: A traditional name for Tirupati, a holy Vaishnavite pilgrimage site.

Veera Narayana Perumal.description: A form of Vishnu worshipped in a temple, likely referring to a temple in Tamil Nadu.

svadharma.description: One's own duty or righteous path, as prescribed by tradition or scripture.

Kedheeswara temple.description: A temple in Mathottam, praised in Tamil Shaivite hymns.

Sakyamuni.description: An epithet for the Buddha, founder of Buddhism.

Sanatana Dharma.description: A term referring to the eternal order or the collective spiritual traditions of Hinduism.

Podhigai Hills.description: A mountain range in southern Tamil Nadu, associated with sages and legends.

Shiva-yogi.description: A yogi devoted to Shiva, often engaged in ascetic practices.

taluk.description: An administrative division or sub-district in India.

copper plates.description: Thin sheets of copper used historically in South India for recording inscriptions and official grants.

inscribed.description: Written or carved (usually on stone or metal) as a permanent record.

genealogy.description: A record or account of the ancestry and lineage of a family or dynasty.

fief.description: A piece of land granted by a ruler to a vassal in exchange for service.

prostrating.description: Lying stretched out on the ground in reverence or submission.

sashtanga namaskaram.description: A full-body prostration involving eight limbs, signifying total surrender or devotion.

Kalamukha.description: A sect within Shaivism known for ascetic practices and distinctive marks.

skull bowl.description: A ritual vessel made from a human skull, used by certain ascetic sects.

matted locks.description: Hair that is allowed to grow long and become tangled, often worn by ascetics.

archana.description: A ritual of offering and chanting names of the deity in Hindu worship.

abhishekam.description: A ritual bathing of the deity with water, milk, or other substances in Hindu worship.

Ponni River.description: The Tamil name for the Kaveri River, revered as a life-giving river in the region.

barge.description: A flat-bottomed boat, often used for ceremonial or leisurely river journeys.

Navaratri.description: A major Hindu festival spanning nine nights, celebrated with rituals, music, and dance in honor of the goddess Durga.

Thanjavur fort.description: The fortified palace complex in Thanjavur, serving as the royal residence and administrative center of the Chola rulers.

Tanjai.description: An alternate name for Thanjavur, used interchangeably in the text.

Sita.description: A legendary figure from the Indian epic Ramayana, renowned for her virtue and devotion.

Nalayini.description: A figure from Hindu legend, renowned for her devotion and fidelity to her husband.

chignon.description: A hairstyle where the hair is twisted into a bun at the back of the head, often adorned with ornaments.

paneer flower.description: A fragrant flower (Tabernaemontana divaricata) commonly used in South Indian garlands and temple offerings.

Rani.description: A title meaning 'queen', used for royal women in India.

Karuvur Thevar.description: A devout Shaivite poet who lived during the Chola period and composed verses praising Thanjai.

Kopparakesari Parantaka.description: A legendary Chola king, grandfather of Sundara Chozhar, famed for his long and victorious reign.

Kannaradevan.description: A king who fought against Parantaka at the battle of Thakkolam.

Pazhuvettaraiyar Kandan Amudhanar.description: The elder of the Pazhuvettaraiyar clan who supported Parantaka Devar and wielded great authority.

Empress Vanamadevi.description: The Maharani, wife of Sundara Chola, who leads the palace women in religious observances.

Parantaka Deva.description: Another name for Kopparakesari Parantaka, a celebrated Chola king.

Kopparakesari Varman.description: A royal title taken by Parantaka, meaning 'lion among kings with copper-colored hair'.

Tungabhadra River.description: A major river in southern India, marking the northern extent of the Chola Empire at its height.

Chittrambalam.description: Refers to the sanctum of the temple at Chidambaram, famous for its golden roof.

Thillai Chidambaram.description: A sacred temple town known for the great Nataraja temple, significant in Shaivism.

Pazhuvettaraiyar clan.description: The extended family and retainers of the Pazhuvettaraiyar chieftains.

Lankan.description: Relating to Lanka (Sri Lanka), often in the context of medicinal herbs or military campaigns.

puranas.description: Ancient Hindu mythological and historical texts, often used as sources for stories and plays.

Natakam.description: A Tamil word meaning 'drama' or 'play', often used as a suffix for the title of a stage production.

Navalo! Naval!.description: A traditional cheer or shout of approval used by audiences in ancient Tamil assemblies.

poojas.description: Ritual worship ceremonies performed in Hindu temples or homes.

sanctum.description: The innermost and most sacred part of a Hindu temple where the main deity is enshrined.

tutelary.description: Serving as a guardian or protector, often used in the context of a deity who protects a clan or family.

Kodumbalur Velirs.description: Noble chieftains from Kodumbalur, historically allied with the Cholas.

Krishna Paramatma.description: A reference to Lord Krishna, an incarnation of Vishnu, often invoked in epic literature.

Sibi.description: A legendary king from Indian mythology, celebrated for his self-sacrifice and justice.

Manu Needhi Cholan.description: A legendary Chola king famed for executing justice even against his own son to uphold dharma.

Buddha.description: The ninth incarnation of Vishnu in some Hindu traditions, founder of Buddhism.

Karaiyar.description: A coastal community from Lanka (Sri Lanka), traditionally engaged in fishing.

Velirs.description: A class of minor chieftains or feudal lords in ancient Tamil country, often allied with major dynasties.

Paramatma.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'supreme soul' or 'supreme spirit', often used to refer to the divine or God.

Aniruddhan.description: A close friend and confidant of Sundara Chozhar, trusted with personal secrets and important tasks.

Umai Nachiyar.description: A mysterious mute woman from the Karaiyar clan, whose spirit is said to haunt Sundara Chozhar.

Kaveri Amman.description: The river goddess personifying the Kaveri, believed to protect devotees.

Kodumbalur Velir.description: A prominent Tamil noble clan, to which Vanathi belongs.

Thalikulathar temple.description: A temple in Thanjavur, referenced as undergoing renovation.

sanyasi.description: A Hindu ascetic or renunciant, one who gives up worldly life.

Periyappa.description: A Tamil term meaning 'elder paternal uncle.'

Arulmozhivarman.description: A prince of the Chola dynasty, later known as Rajaraja Chola I; he is celebrated as the conqueror of Eezham (Sri Lanka).

Vijayadasami.description: A major Hindu festival marking the end of Navaratri, celebrated with various ceremonies and inaugurations.

Purampadi.description: A locality outside the Thanjavur fort, where the hospital inauguration takes place.

Garuda Mandapam.description: A pillared hall dedicated to Garuda, the eagle mount of Lord Vishnu, often found in Vishnu temples.

Viswakarma.description: A community of artisans and craftsmen, traditionally responsible for temple and palace construction and inscriptions.

Oduvamoorthis.description: Temple singers who recite or sing hymns, especially during religious ceremonies.

Mandiramaavadhu Neeru.description: A specific Thevaram hymn sung by Sambandar, believed to have healing powers.

maddalam.description: A traditional South Indian drum used in temple and classical music.

Sambandar Peruman.description: A revered Tamil Saivite saint and poet, composer of Thevaram hymns.

Nallur Mangalam.description: A village granted as a tax-free endowment for the hospital by Kundavai.

Tanjai Purampadi hospital.description: A charitable hospital established in Thanjavur by Kundavai.

Maduraikonda Koiraajakesari Sundara Chol.description: A full royal title of Sundara Chola, meaning 'the lion among kings who conquered Madurai.'

Sivagnana Kandaradithar.description: A former Chola king, father of Madurantaka Devar.

charter.description: A formal document granting rights or privileges, often used for land or endowment grants.

copperplate grant.description: An official record of land grants or endowments, inscribed on copper plates for permanence.

kalams.description: A traditional South Indian measure of grain, especially paddy (rice).

Peruman.description: A respectful honorific used for revered persons, especially saints or deities.

Vadavāru.description: A river or waterway that encircles the fort, serving as a geographical landmark in the narrative.

nāzhigai.description: A traditional Tamil unit of time, roughly equivalent to 24 minutes.

physician’s son.description: The son of the royal physician of Pazhaiyarai, sent by Kundavai on an errand to fetch herbs; he becomes mistakenly suspected as a spy.

Young Queen of Pazhuvoor.description: A title referring to Nandini, denoting her status as the wife of the powerful Pazhuvettaraiyar and her influence in Pazhuvoor.

façade.description: The front face of a building, especially a palace or grand structure.

terrace.description: A flat, open platform on the upper level of a building, often used for viewing or gatherings.

Kalantaka Kandar.description: Also referred to as Kaalandhaka Kandhar or Kaalandhakandar, he is the Younger Pazhuvettaraiyar, a powerful commander and nobleman loyal to the Chola dynasty.

Ashokavana.description: A legendary grove in the Ramayana, said to have been destroyed by Hanuman during his search for Sita.

Vanara.description: A mythical clan of monkey-like beings in Hindu epics, most notably associated with Hanuman in the Ramayana.

Vedic.description: Relating to the Vedas, ancient Hindu scriptures, often used to denote supreme authority or sacredness.

auspicious hour.description: A time considered favorable or lucky for undertaking important actions, determined by astrology.

omen.description: A phenomenon believed to foretell future events, often interpreted as a sign of good or bad luck.

portents.description: Signs or warnings that something, especially something momentous or calamitous, is likely to happen.

realm of Yama.description: The domain of Yama, the Hindu god of death, symbolizing the afterlife or death itself.

Vaani Amma.description: Sendhan Amudhan's mother, who is deaf and mute, living near the lotus pond outside Tanjavur fort.

Thanjai Fort.description: The massive fortress at Tanjavur (Thanjai), serving as the political and military center of the Chola empire.

Pandya dynasty.description: A rival South Indian dynasty, whose lost crown and garland are sought after in the story.

Tiger Hall.description: A chamber within the mint complex where tigers are kept, serving as a deterrent for prison escapes.

mint.description: A place where coins are manufactured under royal authority.

goldsmiths.description: Artisans skilled in working with gold, especially in making ornaments or coins.

garland.description: A decorative wreath or string of flowers, often used in religious offerings or celebrations.

konrai flowers.description: Golden yellow flowers of the Indian laburnum tree, sacred to Lord Shiva and commonly used in worship.

Vanjiammai.description: A respectful term for an elder woman, here referring to Sendhan Amudhan's mother.

Sundara Cholar.description: Sundara Cholar is the ailing emperor of the Chola dynasty and father to Aditya Karikalan, Kundavai, and Arulmozhi Varman.

Hamsathoolika.description: A luxurious couch or swing, often used in royal or noble households in South India.

Kadambur Sambuvarayar palace.description: The palace of Sambuvarayar in Kadambur, a site of significant political intrigue.

Kashi.description: A sacred city in North India, also known as Varanasi, famous for its religious significance.

Brahmaloka.description: In Hindu cosmology, the celestial abode of Brahma, the creator god.

throne.description: A ceremonial chair for a sovereign, but in this context, often refers to royal authority.

treasury chamber.description: A secure room or vault in a palace where valuables and state treasures are kept.

Kalandhagan.description: Kalandhagan is the brother of Pazhuvettarayar, involved in the administration and security of the Chola fortresses.

Anbil Brahmarayar.description: Anbil Brahmarayar is a wise and trusted Brahmin minister in the Chola court, often engaged in diplomatic and secretive missions.

Brahmin.description: A member of the priestly caste in Hindu society, often serving as scholars, priests, or ministers.

Kodumbalur Periya Velar.description: A powerful Chola nobleman and military commander, also known as Boothi Vikrama Kesari, leading the Lankan campaign.

Boothi Vikrama Kesari.description: The same as Kodumbalur Periya Velar, he is the Commander-in-Chief of the Chola forces in Lanka.

Thirugnana Sambandar.description: A revered 7th-century Tamil Shaivite saint and poet, known for his devotional hymns.

Kedheeswarar.description: A form of Lord Shiva worshipped at the Kedheeswarar temple in Maathottam, an important pilgrimage site.

Thirukkedhiswaram.description: A sacred Shaivite temple town in Eelam (Sri Lanka), known for its ancient temple dedicated to Shiva.

Commander-in-Chief.description: The highest-ranking military officer in charge of all armed forces in a campaign or region.

turban.description: A long cloth wound around the head, commonly worn by men in South Asia.

Pillaiyar.description: The Tamil name for Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed Hindu deity, often invoked for auspicious beginnings.

Commander Vikramakesari.description: The chief of the Kodumbalur Velar clan, Commander Vikramakesari is a high-ranking military leader and an important supporter of the Chola royal family.

Vanathi Devi.description: A noblewoman and close companion to Princess Kundavai, Vanathi Devi is gentle and loyal, with her own role in the royal household.

Indra-mala.description: A legendary jeweled garland or crown associated with royalty and divine favor.

Swamiji.description: An honorific used to address or refer to a respected religious ascetic or monk.

Vaishnavar.description: Tamil for 'Vaishnavite', a follower of Vishnu.

palm insignia.description: A symbol or seal made from palm leaves, used as a mark of authority or identification.

Periya Velar.description: Title referring to Boothi Vikrama Kesari, the elder Velar of Kodumbalur and Commander-in-Chief of the Chola forces.

Chinna Velar.description: Younger brother of Boothi Vikrama Kesari from Kodumbalur, who died heroically in battle in Lanka.

Veera Vaishnavar.description: A term for a brave or militant Vaishnavite, here referring to Alwarkadiyan.

Paalavi river.description: A river in the region, whose breached banks have caused flooding and devastation.

signet.description: A seal or emblem used to authenticate documents or denote authority, often worn as a ring.

Oori.description: A jackal that acts as a scout for a leopard during hunting, alerting the leopard to prey with a howl.

sword-belt.description: A belt designed to hold or support a sword at the waist.

Parthibendra Varman.description: A close confidant of Prince Aditya Karikalan from Kanchi, a Pallava nobleman who is wary of Vandiyathevan and involved in Chola politics.

Srivaishnavan.description: A term referring to a follower of the Srivaishnava tradition, a sect of Vaishnavism in South India.

Rajapattai.description: A Tamil term meaning 'royal road' or 'royal highway,' indicating the main road used by royalty and armies.

Simhagiri.description: A fortress and region in Sri Lanka, also known as Sigiriya, important in the context of the Chola-Lankan conflict.

Tamballai.description: A place near the royal highway in Sri Lanka, close to the Chola army's reach.

Buddhist monks.description: Religious ascetics and clergy of Buddhism, significant in Anuradhapura and the region's culture.

Pallava clan.description: A historic South Indian dynasty, here referring to Parthibendra Varman's heritage.

girdle.description: A cloth or belt worn around the waist.

Gajendra.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'lord of elephants,' often used in Hindu mythology to refer to a legendary elephant.

Trishanku’s heaven.description: A reference to a mythical suspended heaven from Hindu legend, symbolizing being caught between worlds.

Vedas.description: The ancient sacred scriptures of Hinduism, considered highly authoritative.

moat.description: A deep, wide ditch surrounding a fort or castle, often filled with water, used for defense.

Amavasya.description: The new moon night in the Hindu lunar calendar, often considered auspicious or suitable for secretive activities.

Mahadeva.description: A name for Lord Shiva, meaning 'Great God' in Sanskrit.

yakshas.description: Nature-spirits or semi-divine beings in Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist traditions.

kinnaras.description: Mythical beings, often depicted as celestial musicians with human and bird-like features.

thazhampu.description: A fragrant flower (screw pine or pandanus) commonly used in South Indian rituals and decorations.

Periya Bikshu.description: A senior Buddhist monk (bhikshu) at the Choodamani Vihara who tends to Ponniyin Selvan and plays a guiding role.

Chinna Bikshu.description: A junior Buddhist monk at the Choodamani Vihara who assists with Ponniyin Selvan's care.

Nandi Mandapam.description: A pavilion or hall dedicated to Nandi, the sacred bull of Shiva, often found in temples and used as a meeting place.

Buddhism.description: A major world religion and philosophy, significant in the story due to the presence of Buddhist monasteries and monks.

Acharyare.description: A respectful term for a spiritual teacher or preceptor, especially in religious contexts.

Amudha.description: A term of endearment or a shortened form of Sendhan Amudhan's name, used affectionately.

Chera Nadu.description: The territory of the Chera dynasty, another ancient Tamil kingdom.

Chandragupta.description: A reference to Chandragupta Maurya, a great emperor of northern India.

Samudra Gupta.description: A powerful Gupta emperor of northern India.

Harshavardhana.description: A notable emperor who ruled northern India in the 7th century.

Mahendra Chakravarthi.description: A Pallava king, known for his patronage of arts and architecture.

Maldives.description: An island nation southwest of India, referenced as part of the Chola imperial vision.

Arulvarma.description: A term of endearment or alternate name for Ponniyin Selvan (Arulmozhi Varman).

Agastya.description: A revered sage in Hindu tradition, often associated with southern India.

Nandideva.description: An honorific for Nandi, the divine bull and gatekeeper of Shiva.

Parameshvara.description: A Sanskrit term meaning 'Supreme Lord,' often referring to Shiva.

Dakshina Meru.description: A mythological reference to the 'Southern Meru,' symbolizing the cosmic mountain and axis of the universe.

Periya Thaayar.description: The elder queen or elder mother, a mute and deaf woman believed to be Arulmozhi Varman's great-aunt.

Buddhist Vihara.description: A monastery or residence for Buddhist monks, indicating the presence of Buddhism in the region during the Chola period.

Rishabarajan.description: The name given to the royal bull in the story, 'Rishaba' meaning bull in Sanskrit and Tamil.

sattvic.description: A Sanskrit term denoting purity, goodness, and harmony, one of the three gunas (qualities) in Hindu philosophy.

Aditya Karikala.description: The crown prince of the Chola dynasty, renowned for his bravery and military prowess; son of Sundara Chola and elder brother to Ponniyin Selvan.

Kedilam.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, India, significant in the region of Thirumunaippadi and the setting for this chapter.

Thiruvathigai Veeratthaanam.description: A sacred temple site on the banks of the Kedilam river, associated with Appar, a revered Tamil Saivite saint.

Thirunavalur.description: A town near the Kedilam river, famous as the home of Sundaramurthi, another important Saivite saint.

Kopparakesari.description: An honorific title borne by Chola kings, meaning 'lion among kings'.

Chola Maharaja.description: A royal title meaning 'Great King of the Cholas'.

Parantaka Chakravartin.description: A former Chola emperor, known for his military achievements and expansion of the empire.

conch-blowers.description: Individuals who blow conch shells, often to announce the arrival of royalty or during religious ceremonies.

Munaiyadaraiyar.description: The chieftain of Thirumunaippadi, an ally of the Cholas.

Ganges.description: A major river in northern India, symbolizing the northern extent of imperial ambition.

Nambi Arurar.description: Another name for Sundaramurthi Adigal, a revered Tamil Shaivite saint.

South Pennai.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, also known as the Ponnaiyar, important for the region's geography.

Kaikkolars.description: A famous warrior regiment in the Chola army.

Navalo Naval.description: A traditional war cry or chant used by Chola soldiers.

Vritrasura.description: A demon slain by Indra in Hindu mythology.

Ganga Nadu.description: A kingdom in southern India, ruled by the Ganga dynasty.

Maniyakedam.description: The capital city of the Twin Realms (Rashtrakutas).

Pallava dynasty.description: A major South Indian dynasty preceding the Cholas.

Vellaru.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, mentioned as a site for military encampment.

banner.description: A flag or standard, especially one bearing a symbol or emblem of a dynasty or army.

Rajaraja.description: Refers to Rajaraja Chola I, one of the greatest Chola emperors, celebrated for his conquests and temple-building.

Parantaka Chakravarti.description: A former Chola emperor, known for expanding the Chola kingdom and his many marriages.

umbrella.description: A symbol of royal authority and sovereignty in South Indian tradition, representing kingship.

Anantha Battar.description: A Vaishnavite scholar from Thirunarayanapuram, reputed for his debating prowess.

Kedila River.description: A river mentioned as the setting for part of the chapter, possibly a tributary of the Kaveri.

Thirukanaattumulloor.description: A village on the northern bank of the Kollidam river, known for its temples.

Kanaattumulloor.description: The location of a Shiva temple where festival rituals are performed.

Thirunarayanapuram.description: A sacred Vaishnavite pilgrimage center, home to the scholar Anantha Battar.

Saktas.description: Followers of Shaktism, a tradition that worships the goddess Shakti.

naaval tree.description: A tropical tree (Syzygium cumini) whose wood is used for staffs and whose fruit is considered auspicious.

kadamba tree.description: A flowering tree native to South Asia, often found near temples and sacred sites.

neem tree.description: A medicinal tree (Azadirachta indica) revered in Indian tradition for its purifying properties.

Sri Vaishnavites.description: Members of the Sri Vaishnava sect, a prominent Vaishnavite tradition founded by Ramanuja.

Haridwar.description: A major pilgrimage city in North India, considered one of the holiest places for Hindus.

Ayyanar temple.description: A rural temple dedicated to Ayyanar, a guardian deity worshipped in Tamil villages.

clay horses.description: Terracotta horses offered as votive gifts to Ayyanar, symbolizing devotion and requests for protection.

acharyas.description: Spiritual preceptors or teachers, especially within the Vaishnavite tradition.

loincloths.description: A simple garment worn around the waist, typical attire for ascetics or commoners in ancient India.

upper garment.description: A cloth draped over the shoulders or upper body, part of traditional South Indian dress.

festoon.description: A decorative chain or garland of flowers, leaves, or ribbons, used for festival adornment.

signet rings.description: Rings bearing a seal or emblem, used to authenticate documents or denote authority.

turban cloth.description: A long piece of cloth wound around the head, traditionally worn by men in South India.

trapdoor.description: A hinged or removable panel in a floor or ceiling, providing access to a hidden space or passage.

bangles.description: Traditional rigid bracelets, usually made of metal, glass, or wood, worn by women in India.

kuravai-koothu.description: Another term for the Kuravai dance, emphasizing its dramatic and performative aspects.

Paranthaman.description: A reference to Vishnu, often used in Tamil devotional contexts.

Sundaramurthi Nayanar.description: A renowned Tamil Saivite saint and poet, famous for composing devotional hymns to Lord Shiva during his pilgrimages.

Manimuktha River.description: A river in Tamil Nadu, significant in the region's geography and referenced in the journey of the characters.

Baalambikai.description: A form of the goddess consecrated at the temple, meaning 'Young Mother,' to inspire Sundaramurthi Nayanar to compose hymns.

Abhimanyu.description: A legendary young warrior from the Mahabharata, symbolizing youthful heroism and valor.

Chithra Mandapam.description: A hall or pavilion in the Thanjavur palace, adorned with portraits of Chola ancestors.

Yamaloka.description: In Hindu belief, the realm of Yama, the god of death; often referred to as the afterlife or the abode of departed souls.

kovai.description: A small, red fruit native to South India, also known as ivy gourd.

Sita Devi.description: Sita Devi is a revered figure from the Hindu epic Ramayana, known for her virtue and suffering, often referenced as an ideal of womanhood.

cot.description: A light, portable bed or couch, often used in South Asian households.

censer.description: A vessel in which incense is burned, commonly used in religious or ceremonial contexts.

swayamvaram.description: An ancient Indian practice where a woman chooses her husband from among a group of suitors, often through a public ceremony.

garlanding.description: The act of placing a garland (a wreath of flowers) around someone's neck, often as a sign of honor or in marriage ceremonies.

Nappinnai.description: A gopika (milkmaid) and beloved of Krishna in Tamil devotional literature.

machu path.description: A walkway or path along the fort walls, typically used for patrolling or moving between sections of a fortress.

Kannara.description: Refers to the twin regions or territories conquered by the Cholas, possibly in Karnataka.

Pazhaiyaarai.description: An ancient Chola capital and royal seat.

Parantaka Sundara Chozha Chakravarthi.description: The full royal title of Emperor Sundara Chola.

Arinjaya Thevar.description: A Chola king, father of Sundara Chola, noted for his valor.

Killi Valavan.description: A Chola king known for building seventy-two Shiva temples.

Koperun Cholan.description: A notable Chola king in the royal lineage.

Nalangilli.description: A Chola king mentioned in the royal lineage.

Nedungkilli.description: A Chola king mentioned in the royal lineage.

Sittpuli Nadu.description: A region marking the extent of Chola rule.

Kolli Hills.description: A mountain range in Tamil Nadu, associated with Valvil Ori.

herald.description: An official messenger or announcer, especially one who makes royal proclamations.

padar, padar.description: Onomatopoeic Tamil phrase imitating the sound of doors or gates slamming shut.

Kolli Malai.description: A hill region in Tamil Nadu, associated with the legendary chieftain Valvil Ori.

maidservants.description: Female domestic workers who serve in royal or noble households.

hymns.description: Sacred songs or chants, often in praise of deities, commonly recited in temples.

Anni.description: Tamil term for 'sister-in-law,' specifically one's elder brother's wife.

Thirunavukkarasar.description: A revered Tamil Shaivite saint and poet, known for his devotional hymns to Lord Shiva.

nursemaids.description: Women employed to care for and attend to children or female members of a household.

Paramananda.description: Paramananda is a disciple of Aniruddha, who brings news and information to the court.

Ilaiyarani.description: A Tamil term meaning 'young queen' or 'junior queen'.

pasuram.description: A Tamil devotional hymn, especially those composed by the Alvar saints.

discus weapon.description: Refers to the 'chakra', a spinning, disk-like weapon associated with the deity Vishnu (Thirumal).
